scope: Engine-light localized message identity, BCP 47 locale fallback, an ICU MessageFormat subset, CLDR cardinal plural categories, and content validation, with a thin Unity adapter planned separately
review_note: The URLs below were not fetched from the authoring environment because its network egress policy blocks them; the admitted claims come from the author's prior reading of these specifications and must be confirmed by a person before the admission record is signed.

sources.license_or_terms: IETF Trust document terms; syntax facts only
sources.maintenance_evidence: BCP 47 is the current Internet standard for language tags; not fetched from this environment
sources.admitted_role: Locale identity syntax: language, script, and region subtags and their canonical casing
admitted_claims: A language tag is a sequence of subtags separated by hyphens with a primary language subtag first
Script subtags are four letters and region subtags are two letters or three digits
Tags are case-insensitive; conventional casing is lowercase language, titlecase script, uppercase region
excluded_uses: Core does not implement extended language, variant, extension, or private-use subtags
No claim of full BCP 47 validation against the IANA registry

sources.license_or_terms: IETF Trust document terms; algorithm facts only
sources.maintenance_evidence: RFC 4647 is the current BCP 47 matching specification; not fetched from this environment
sources.admitted_role: Fallback chain construction by progressive truncation of the requested tag
admitted_claims: Lookup finds the best single match by removing subtags from the end of the range until a match is found
A default value is returned when no truncation matches
excluded_uses: Filtering and extended filtering are not implemented

sources.license_or_terms: Unicode License; rule facts only, no data files copied
sources.maintenance_evidence: CLDR plural rules are the reference used by ICU and major platforms; not fetched from this environment
sources.admitted_role: Cardinal plural categories and the operands n, i, and v for the declared language set
admitted_claims: Plural categories are zero, one, two, few, many, and other, and other is always present
Rules are expressed over operands such as the absolute value, integer digits, and visible fraction digits
Languages differ in which categories they use; English uses one and other, Russian one, few, many, other, Arabic all six, Japanese other only
excluded_uses: Ordinal rules, range rules, and compact-number many rules added in later CLDR releases are not implemented
Languages outside the declared set are reported as unsupported, not approximated

sources.license_or_terms: ICU documentation terms; syntax facts only, no ICU code copied
sources.maintenance_evidence: ICU MessageFormat is the widely adopted message syntax that platform localization tools accept; not fetched from this environment
sources.admitted_role: Template syntax: named arguments, plural and select branches, the # number sign, exact =n selectors, apostrophe quoting
admitted_claims: Arguments are written in braces with an optional type and style
plural and select arguments carry named branches and must include an other branch
A number sign inside a plural branch is replaced by the formatted number
An apostrophe quotes syntax characters and two apostrophes produce one
excluded_uses: Date, time, number-style, spellout, ordinal, and choice arguments are not implemented
No claim of full ICU compatibility

sources.license_or_terms: Unity documentation terms; architecture facts only
sources.maintenance_evidence: Unity Localization is the engine's maintained localization package; version pin to be confirmed by a person
sources.admitted_role: Adapter boundary: string tables keyed by locale, locale fallback, and smart-string formatting as the engine-side counterpart
admitted_claims: The engine package separates locales, string tables, and table entries keyed by a stable key
Locale fallback is configurable per locale
Smart Strings provide placeholder and plural formatting on the engine side
excluded_uses: Core does not depend on the Unity Localization package; the adapter may bridge to it when present
No claim about the engine package's runtime behavior without a compatibility profile

sources.license_or_terms: Epic documentation terms; architecture facts only
sources.maintenance_evidence: Unreal Engine localization is a shipped, maintained second-engine implementation; not fetched from this environment
sources.admitted_role: Independent evidence that text identity (namespace and key), culture fallback, and a gather-translate-compile pipeline are the common kernel
admitted_claims: Text identity is separate from its translations and stable across edits
Culture fallback walks from specific to general cultures
excluded_uses: No Unreal type, asset format, or tool is copied

sources.license_or_terms: Apache-2.0 documentation and reference implementations; design facts only
sources.maintenance_evidence: Fluent ships in Firefox and has independent implementations in several languages; not fetched from this environment
sources.admitted_role: Counterexample and design boundary: asymmetric localization where translators own plural and grammatical variation
admitted_claims: Translations may need branches the source language does not, so validation must be per target locale
Fallback to a source locale must be explicit and reported rather than silent
excluded_uses: Fluent syntax is not implemented; the MessageFormat subset is the admitted syntax

source_gate_non_claims: No source grants package maturity, release, certification, or platform authority
The first implementation is a message-formatting and validation substrate, not a complete localization pipeline or editor
The declared plural language set is a subset of CLDR and is stated in the code; any other language is unsupported until its rules are added with tests
